Create a new user account (driver or fleet_manager).
Authenticate a user and return a JWT token.
List vehicles with pagination, searchable by license_plate, make, and model. Supports filter by status.
Retrieve details of a specific vehicle by its ID.
Create a new vehicle record. Requires license_plate, make, model, year, and status.
Update an existing vehicle's information.
Delete a vehicle record.
List all users with pagination. Accessible only by fleet_manager role.
Get a specific user's profile.
Create a new user (used by registration endpoint).
Update user details such as role or activation status.
Remove a user from the system.
List trip requests with pagination. Supports filter by status and date range.
Retrieve a specific trip request by ID.
Driver creates a new vehicle request. Validates start_date < end_date.
Fleet manager approves or rejects a trip request and updates its status.
Cancel a trip request.
List maintenance records with pagination. Supports filter by vehicle_id and date range.
Get details of a specific maintenance record.
Log a new maintenance event for a vehicle.
Update an existing maintenance record.
Delete a maintenance record.

features: Create, read, update, and list vehicles with status tracking.
Drivers submit requests; managers approve or reject; vehicle status updates accordingly.
Log maintenance events, calculate total cost per vehicle, and set vehicle status to maintenance.

user_stories.want: to register a new vehicle with its details
acceptance_criteria: A vehicle record is created when all required fields (license_plate, make, model, year, status) are supplied.
The system returns a 201 response with the vehicle ID and stored data.
The new vehicle appears in the vehicle list with status "available".

user_stories.want: to request a vehicle for a specific trip
acceptance_criteria: The request endpoint validates start_date < end_date and required fields (vehicle_id, purpose).
A pending trip request is created with status "pending" and linked to the driver.
The driver receives a confirmation email (simulated) with request details.

user_stories.want: to approve a driver’s vehicle request
acceptance_criteria: Approving a request changes its status to "approved" and updates the vehicle status to "in_use" for the requested dates.
The system prevents approving overlapping requests for the same vehicle.
An approval notification is sent to the driver.

user_stories.want: to reject a driver’s vehicle request
acceptance_criteria: Rejecting a request changes its status to "rejected" and leaves the vehicle status unchanged.
The driver receives a rejection notification with an optional reason.
The rejected request is still visible in the driver’s trip history with status "rejected".

user_stories.want: to log a maintenance record for a vehicle
acceptance_criteria: A maintenance record is created when date, description, and cost are provided.
The vehicle status automatically switches to "maintenance" for the maintenance date range.
The total maintenance cost for a vehicle can be retrieved via a summary endpoint.

user_stories.want: to view my trip history
acceptance_criteria: The trip history endpoint returns only trips belonging to the authenticated driver.
Each trip entry includes vehicle details, dates, purpose, and final status.
Results are paginated with a default page size of 20.

user_stories.want: to view total maintenance cost per vehicle
acceptance_criteria: A summary endpoint returns vehicle_id, license_plate, and sum(cost) of all maintenance records.
The endpoint filters out vehicles with no maintenance records.
The response is sorted descending by total cost.

user_stories.want: to see which vehicles are currently available
acceptance_criteria: The vehicle list endpoint returns only vehicles with status "available" for the requested date range.
Search parameters (license_plate, make) filter the list correctly.
Pagination is applied with a maximum of 50 items per page.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required - all endpoints must be accessed by an authenticated user to protect fleet data.
non_functional_requirements.authorization: role-based: fleet_manager can create vehicles, approve/reject requests, and log maintenance; driver can only request vehicles and view own trips.
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on vehicle list, trip list, and maintenance list endpoints.
non_functional_requirements.search: vehicles can be searched by license_plate, make, and model.
non_functional_requirements.file_uploads: no - maintenance records are textual only.
non_functional_requirements.real_time: no - updates are reflected on next API call; real‑time push not needed.

generic.idea: A hospital management system. Manages departments, doctors, nurses, patients, admissions, bed allocation, surgery scheduling, lab results, pharmacy dispensing, and insurance billing.

api_endpoints.description: Populate the database with demo data for patients, beds, admissions, and users.
Return aggregate counts such as total patients, occupied beds, and active admissions for dashboard overview.
Create a new user account with role assignment.
Authenticate a user and return a JWT access token.
Retrieve the currently authenticated user's profile.
Search and list patients; supports ?search=, ?limit=, ?offset= for pagination.
Get detailed information for a specific patient.
Create a new patient record.
Replace an existing patient record with the supplied data.
Delete a patient record.
List beds with optional search (e.g., by ward) and pagination.
Retrieve details of a specific bed.
Create a new bed record.
Update an existing bed's information.
Remove a bed from the system.
List admissions with search, pagination, and optional filters.
Get full details of a specific admission, including patient and bed info.
Create a new admission, assigning a patient to a free bed.
Replace an admission record (e.g., change diagnosis or reassign bed).
Discharge a patient by setting discharge_date; automatically frees the bed.
Delete an admission record.

features: Create, read, update, and search patient records.
Create, view, paginate, and discharge admissions, linking patients to beds.

user_stories.want: to create a new admission for a patient and assign a free bed
acceptance_criteria: POST /admissions returns 201 with a generated admission_id
The created admission record contains patient_id, bed_id, and admission_date
The assigned bed's is_occupied flag is set to true

user_stories.want: to view a paginated list of current admissions
acceptance_criteria: GET /admissions?page=1&size=20 returns a paginated response with total count
Each item includes patient name, bed location, and admission date
Changing page or size parameters returns the correct slice of data

user_stories.want: to discharge a patient
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /admissions/{id} with discharge_date sets the field on the admission
The related bed's is_occupied flag is automatically set to false
GET /admissions/{id} shows a non‑null discharge_date

user_stories.want: to view a patient’s admission details
acceptance_criteria: GET /admissions/{id} returns patient full name, diagnosis, bed ward/room, and dates
The endpoint is accessible only to authenticated users with role doctor or admin
If the admission does not exist, the API returns 404

user_stories.want: to search for patients by name
acceptance_criteria: GET /patients?search=smith returns all patients whose name contains 'smith' case‑insensitively
Partial matches are supported (e.g., 'jo' matches 'John')
If no matches are found, an empty list is returned with 200 status

user_stories.want: to add a new patient record
acceptance_criteria: POST /patients with required fields (name, dob, gender, contact) returns 201 and patient_id
Missing required fields cause a 400 response with a validation error message
The new patient appears in subsequent GET /patients searches

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — all endpoints must be accessed by an authenticated user
non_functional_requirements.authorization: role‑based: admin (full access), clerk (patient & admission CRUD), doctor (read‑only admission view)
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on GET /admissions
non_functional_requirements.search: required on GET /patients (name search)

user_stories.want: to log in securely to my CRM account
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the login page, when I enter valid credentials and click 'Login', then I am redirected to my contacts dashboard.
Given I am on the login page, when I enter invalid credentials and click 'Login', then I see an error message 'Invalid credentials'.

user_stories.want: to add a new contact with their details
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the contacts page, when I click 'Add Contact' and fill in name, email, phone, company, and select a status, then the new contact appears in my contact list.
Given I am adding a new contact, when I leave a required field (e.g., name) blank, then I see a validation error and the contact is not created.

user_stories.want: to add a note to a contact
acceptance_criteria: Given I am viewing a contact's details, when I enter text into the 'Add Note' field and click 'Save Note', then the note appears in the contact's notes section with a timestamp.
Given a contact has multiple notes, when I view the contact's details, then the notes are displayed in chronological order (newest first).

user_stories.want: to log an interaction (call, email, meeting) with a contact
acceptance_criteria: Given I am viewing a contact's details, when I select an interaction type (Call, Email, Meeting), a date, and an outcome, then the interaction is added to the contact's interaction log.
Given a contact has logged interactions, when I view the contact's details, then the interactions are displayed chronologically with type, date, and outcome.

user_stories.want: to see my contacts grouped by their status in a pipeline view
acceptance_criteria: Given I navigate to the 'Pipeline' view, then I see distinct sections for 'Lead', 'Prospect', 'Customer', and 'Churned' contacts.
Given I have contacts with different statuses, when I view the pipeline, then each status section displays the correct count of contacts assigned to that status.

user_stories.want: to search for contacts by name or company
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the contacts list, when I type 'John' into the search bar, then only contacts with 'John' in their name are displayed.
Given I am on the contacts list, when I type 'Acme Corp' into the search bar, then only contacts associated with 'Acme Corp' are displayed.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — users need to log in to access their private contact data.
non_functional_requirements.authorization: Users can only access and manage their own contacts and associated data.
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on contacts list if the number of contacts exceeds a reasonable display limit (e.g., 50).
non_functional_requirements.search: contacts (by name, company)

Show enrollment counts per course and enable dropping a student
List a student's current enrollments and compute total semester credits

user_stories.want: to create a new course with code, title, credits, instructor, capacity, and semester
acceptance_criteria: A POST /courses request with all required fields returns 201 Created and the course appears in GET /courses
If any required field is missing, the API returns 400 Bad Request with a descriptive error
The created course's capacity is stored and cannot be negative

user_stories.want: to view enrollment counts for each of my courses
acceptance_criteria: GET /courses returns a list where each course object includes an "enrolled_count" field
The "enrolled_count" equals the number of Enrollment records linked to that course
Counts update in real‑time after any enrollment or drop operation

user_stories.want: to drop a student from a specific course
acceptance_criteria: DELETE /enrollments/{enrollment_id} returns 204 No Content when the enrollment exists
After deletion, GET /courses/{course_id} shows a decremented "enrolled_count"
The dropped student no longer appears in GET /students/{student_id}/enrollments

user_stories.want: to browse the course catalog filtered by semester
acceptance_criteria: GET /courses?semester=Fall2025 returns only courses with semester = "Fall2025"
Each course object includes code, title, credits, instructor, capacity, and current enrollment count
Pagination is applied when more than 20 courses match the filter

user_stories.want: to enroll in a course that still has open seats
acceptance_criteria: POST /enrollments with valid student_id and course_id returns 201 Created when enrollment_count < capacity
The response includes the new enrollment record with a unique id
If the course is full, the API returns 409 Conflict with a message "Course capacity reached"

user_stories.want: to view all courses I am enrolled in and see my total credit load
acceptance_criteria: GET /students/{student_id}/enrollments returns a list of enrolled courses with their credit values
The response also includes a "total_credits" field that sums the credits of all returned courses
If the student has no enrollments, the list is empty and total_credits = 0

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required - protect all endpoints with JWT
non_functional_requirements.authorization: role‑based: Registrars can manage courses and enrollments; Students can only view catalog, enroll, and view their own enrollments
non_functional_requirements.pagination: required on GET /courses and GET /students/{id}/enrollments
non_functional_requirements.search: course catalog filtering by semester (and optional keyword search)
non_functional_requirements.real_time: no - consistency is achieved via immediate DB writes

features: Create, read, update, and delete student records with name, grade, and enrollment date

Teachers enter assignment scores for students, storing assignment name, score, and max score
Admins and teachers have distinct permissions for data access and mutation

user_stories.want: to register a new student with name, grade, and enrollment date
acceptance_criteria: When the admin submits a valid form, a student record is created and returned with a unique ID
The API returns a 400 error if any required field (name, grade, enrollment_date) is missing
The new student is searchable via the student search endpoint within 2 seconds

user_stories.want: to create and edit a class (name, subject, assigned teacher)
acceptance_criteria: Creating a class returns a class object containing the assigned teacher's user ID
Updating a class changes only the supplied fields and leaves others unchanged
Deleting a class that has associated records returns a 400 error unless a force‑delete flag is used

user_stories.want: to record attendance for a class session
acceptance_criteria: The teacher can submit a list of student IDs with a status of present or absent for a given class and date
The system stores one attendance record per student per class per date and returns a 201 status
Attempting to record attendance for a future date returns a 400 validation error

user_stories.want: to enter grades for an assignment
acceptance_criteria: The teacher provides assignment name, max score, and each student's score; the API creates a grade record for each student
Scores greater than the max score are rejected with a 422 error
Grades are immutable after 24 hours unless the teacher has an admin override flag

user_stories.want: to view a student's overall attendance rate across all classes
acceptance_criteria: The attendance summary endpoint returns a percentage (present days / total recorded days) rounded to two decimals
If a student has no attendance records, the rate is reported as 0% rather than an error
The response includes a breakdown by class for deeper insight

user_stories.want: to view a student's grade summary across classes
acceptance_criteria: The grade summary endpoint returns the average score (weighted by max score) for each class and an overall average
Grades with missing scores are excluded from the average calculation
The endpoint supports an optional query parameter `as_of` to compute the summary up to a specific date

user_stories.want: to view the roster of students for a class they teach
acceptance_criteria: The roster endpoint returns a list of student IDs, names, and current grade level
Only teachers assigned to the class can access its roster; others receive a 403 error
The list is paginated with a default page size of 25

user_stories.want: to search for students by name or grade
acceptance_criteria: The search endpoint supports partial, case‑insensitive matches on name and exact matches on grade
Results are returned within 1 second for a dataset of up to 10,000 students
Pagination parameters `page` and `page_size` are respected

user_stories.want: to edit a student's basic information (name, grade, enrollment date)
acceptance_criteria: Updating a student returns the modified student object with the new values
Changing the enrollment date to a future date is rejected with a 422 error
Audit fields `updated_at` and `updated_by` are populated on every edit

Agents cannot change the status of listings they do not own

user_stories.want: to search listings by price range, number of bedrooms, and location

user_stories.want: to save a listing as a favorite

user_stories.want: to request a viewing for a specific listing

user_stories.want: to view all pending viewing requests for my listings

user_stories.want: to confirm or decline a viewing request

acceptance_criteria: POST /api/employees returns 201 and the created employee JSON with a generated id

user_stories.want: to edit an existing employee’s details
acceptance_criteria: PUT /api/employees/{id} with valid fields returns 200 and the updated employee JSON
Changes are reflected in a following GET /api/employees/{id}
Attempting to update a non‑existent employee returns 404

user_stories.want: to mark an employee as inactive when they leave
acceptance_criteria: PATCH /api/employees/{id}/deactivate returns 200 and sets active = false
Inactive employees are excluded from the default GET /api/employees list unless a query param include_inactive=true is supplied
Deactivating an already inactive employee returns 400 with an appropriate error message

user_stories.want: to search the directory by employee name
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/employees?search=John returns a 200 list containing only employees whose name contains 'John' (case‑insensitive)
Results are paginated with a default page size of 20
Only active employees are returned unless include_inactive=true is specified

user_stories.want: to filter the directory by department
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/employees?department=Engineering returns 200 with employees whose department field equals 'Engineering'
The filter works together with name search (both query params can be combined)
Pagination applies to filtered results as well

user_stories.want: to view an org chart for any employee
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/employees/{id}/org-chart returns 200 with a JSON tree of manager → direct reports recursively
The root node matches the requested employee id
If the employee has no manager, the manager field is null; if no reports, the reports array is empty
